title: CS amp, current-source load
description: Common-source stage with a current-source load: the canonical $g_m/I_D$ first sheet. $g_m$ is fixed from the bandwidth spec (with an explicit over-design factor), $g_m/I_D$ is the efficiency knob, and the load device is a composed child so its output conductance and noise enter the gain and noise budgets honestly. Pick the load child's device table to the opposite polarity (set load_sign to -1 for a signed-PMOS table).

params.name: V_out
params.note: output DC level; sets both devices' operating vds

params.name: cdd_est
params.note: output-node parasitic estimate (both drains + wiring); refine from extraction

params.name: gbw_margin
params.note: over-design factor on gm for parasitics and PVT

params.name: gm_id
params.note: input inversion: high = efficient/slow, low = fast/thirsty

params.name: L_load
params.note: longer load L raises the load's output resistance (and the gain)

params.name: gm_id_load
params.note: load inversion: lower gm/ID costs headroom but adds less noise (noise scales with the load's gm)

params.name: load_sign
params.note: vds sign convention of the load table: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

doc.title: Current-source load device
doc.description: One device biased as a current source: carries the stage current at a declared vds, exposing its output conductance, transconductance (its drain-noise scale), and saturation headroom.

params.name: vds_ld
params.note: signed to this device table's axis convention

rows.name: Av
rows.note: both devices' output conductances load the gain

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: the load's 4kTgamma*gm drain noise referred to the input by 1/gm_in

rules.note: gm/ID cannot exceed the weak-inversion ceiling of the data
input device saturated at the output DC level
load device saturated: its headroom is the supply minus the output level
actual GBW into CL plus the parasitic estimate; the over-design factor should keep this green
